newsitem.title: USA: EDS sees momentum going into 1997.
newsitem.headline: EDS sees momentum going into 1997.

text.p: Electronic Data Systems Corp's chief financial officer, Jody Grant, said that the computer services company has "a lot of momentum" going into 1997 and he is "very encouraged" looking at the bookings the company has in the pipeline.
"We think 1997 will be a very good year in terms of bookings," Grant told a Goldman Sachs Technology Conference.
He said the company may exceed its previous record of bookings achieved in 1995 of $10.1 billion.
Grant also said that Electronic Data will begin to target acquisitions, adding that during 1996 the company was too involved in spinning out from General Motors Corp to pursue any deals.
He said in previous years the company has pursued deals at a pace of about six to 12 a year, which added $200-$300 million to its top line.
Electronic Data "will be very aggressive" about pursuing more lower profit-margin businesses in 1997, Grant said.
